parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with payroll, so at the level of the concern they belong together. The problem is that they reach storage in two different ways. PayrollService only talks to repositories (EmployeeRepository, TimesheetRepository) through their own methods (byId, create, approve, forWeek, active), and turns the records it gets back into domain objects (Employee, Timesheet, Payslip). PayrollAuditService skips that repository style. It is handed the raw PrismaService and calls the ORM delegate itself (prisma.payrollAudit.create / findMany). It also builds storage details inside the business service: the record id from `${Date.now()}-${subject}` and the `at` timestamp. So the module has no single way of accessing storage. One service hides persistence behind repositories, and the other writes ORM queries directly. This is a mismatch of abstraction inside the module, not a question of which way the imports point. A smaller, secondary issue: PayrollService rebuilds a Timesheet from a stored record in exactly the same way in two places, `new Timesheet(r.id, r.employeeId, r.week, r.hours, r.approved)` in both approve() and run(). That rebuilding logic should live in one place, such as a factory.

violations.message: Skips the module's repository style: it depends on the raw PrismaService and calls prisma.payrollAudit.create/findMany directly, and it builds the record id and timestamp itself. Its sibling PayrollService only uses repository methods (EmployeeRepository, TimesheetRepository).
The same record-to-Timesheet rebuilding `new Timesheet(r.id, r.employeeId, r.week, r.hours, r.approved)` appears in both approve() and run() rather than in one shared factory or mapper.
